transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I'd like to get our pre-lock round-robin started so we can move toward final production approval on the gala broadcast package. As a reminder, the current draft uses three cameras, includes archive reuse rights, has a sponsor product display on stage, and carries a general caption feed. Before I can sign off, I need each of you — technical, rights, talent, and accessibility leads — to report your final operating requirements. Let's start whenever you're ready.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical technical finding from my RF survey. Wireless roaming camera links interfere with the Orpheum Theater's assistive-listening loop. The gala must use three fixed wired cameras from the marked camera platforms. I filed the survey in the technical folder, but it's not on Mara's draft lock sheet yet. This means the current three-camera plan is fine, but they must be fixed wired cameras on the designated platforms — no wireless roaming.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have a critical rights issue to flag. I received the countersigned performance license this morning, and it permits the gala broadcast but explicitly prohibits any video-on-demand release or later promotional clips. The recording must be marked broadcast-only. This directly conflicts with the current draft package's provision permitting the recording to be reused in the festival archive. I have not yet entered this restriction in the rights tracker, but the archive reuse must be removed from the package before approval. The recording can be used for the broadcast only — no VOD, no promotional clips, no archive reuse.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I have two critical talent requirements to flag. First, I confirmed with the headliner's agent that the performer can soundcheck only at exactly 3:00 PM on Saturday — this is not yet reflected in the production schedule. Second, the headliner's rider explicitly prohibits sponsor product placement anywhere on the performance stage. I have the agent's confirmation in email, but it hasn't been entered into the production schedule yet. This directly conflicts with the current draft package's sponsor product display on stage — that must be removed before approval.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I have a critical accessibility requirement to flag. My caption vendor confirmed that the live caption feed requires the captioner to work from Booth B — its dedicated return feed is connected to the gala's caption encoder. The general plan's control-room location will not work for the caption feed. I documented the vendor confirmation in the accessibility file, but I have not yet added the booth assignment to the lock sheet. This means Booth B must be assigned for the live captioner before approval.
transcript.speaker: A5
